analyst_view.overall: Hamburg (12th) host Bayern (2nd) a week after a 4-0 Nordderby defeat at Werder Bremen; left-back Miro Muheim hurt his calf there and is out for now, on top of Lokonga, Nadir, Remberg, Poulsen and Torunarigha. Bayern are badly hit: Harry Kane (syndesmosis, out for months), Michael Olise (bruised foot), Manuel Neuer, Serge Gnabry, Ismael Saibari and Alphonso Davies are all out, while Luis Díaz is back in the squad after a hamstring tear. The numbers now count all the listed absences, taking about 39% off Bayern's goals, which is more than the 13% I took off yesterday, so I drop my goals cut. Bayern also play at Lille in the Champions League on Wednesday evening, then travel to Hamburg for Saturday. The shots counts still lean on Bayern's recent run with Kane and Olise, so I keep a small trim there; no referee is named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals, 2.0 of them Bayern's, and now take Kane (about -15%), Olise (-14%), Saibari, Gnabry and Davies off Bayern, plus Poulsen and Lokonga off Hamburg. That is already below the 3.4 I called yesterday, so I drop my -13% to avoid counting the injuries twice. Díaz's return and Hamburg losing Muheim help Bayern a little, Bayern's Wednesday trip to Lille works the other way, so I stay at 2.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners. Bayern will still have most of the ball and pin Hamburg back, and fewer wide attackers (Olise, Gnabry, Davies out) could mean a little less crossing, but Hamburg's back three without Muheim may concede more down the flanks. Nothing clear either way, so I stay at 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards, already lifting them slightly for past meetings and trimming for Bayern's calm recent record. Hamburg will want a reaction after the derby defeat, but no referee is named yet and nothing points clearly up or down, so I stay at 4.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 32.3 shots and already add 14% for Bayern's high recent shot count, which came with Kane and Olise in the side; their absences are counted on goals but not on shots. Bayern should still dominate but create a bit less, two and a half days after a Champions League away game, so I take 6% off, to about 30.4.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.7 shots on target, 7.1 of them Bayern's, without taking off Kane and Olise, their most accurate shooters (the injuries are counted only on goals). With Díaz back I trim a little less than yesterday's 10%: 8% off, to about 9.8.
